newsitem.title: THAILAND: U.S. First Lady decries trafficking of girls for sex.
newsitem.headline: U.S. First Lady decries trafficking of girls for sex.

text.p: U.S. First Lady Hillary Clinton on Monday called for continued efforts to end the trafficking of girls for sex and Thai women said they hoped her high profile would help raise awareness of the problem.

Mrs Clinton was on the last day of a two-day visit to two northern Thai cities where she has visted several projects aimed at improving the education of girls and preventing them from being lured into prostitution.
She has focused on women's and children's issues during her visit to a region that is one of the country's biggest markets for prostitution procurement.

"We are all troubled around the world by the rise of international gangs that traffic young girls for sex throughout Asia and the world," Mrs Clinton said in a speech at Chiang Mai University on Monday.

She said the programmes she visited during her stay were important steps towards improving the problem of child prostitution and child labour in Thailand, a popular destination for western paedophiles.
Her comments were applauded by women who said they hoped Mrs Clinton's high profile would help draw attention to problems faced by them and others.

Mee Chay, a 20-year-old AIDS patient, arrived in a wheelchair to see Mrs Clinton during her visit to one of the women's projects and asked her through a translator to help prevent other young girls from suffering her fate.
Mee Chay was an orphan from one of the hilltribe ethnic groups and was sold to a brothel at the age of five, where she was raised to look after prostitutes' children.
She was forced to offer sex services when she was 12, then escaped at the age of 17 but was returned to the same brothel and contracted HIV, the deadly virus that causes AIDS.
When Mee Chay became very ill, she was dumped at the House of Love, a project which provides housing and medical care for tribal women and children who have no homes or family.
"I'm glad that she came here. I wish she would help save other women," Mee Chay said after Mrs Clinton visited the project.

In Chiang Rai, a girl in the "Thai Women for Tomorrow Program", a project sponsored in part by the United States which works on educating girls to keep them out of the sex trade, asked Mrs Clinton to support the project and others like it.
Thailand's public and private sectors have launched several other programmes to promote welfare for women and children.
But many think that Mrs Clinton's voice will put a brighter spotlight on the plight of children and women.
"I think this is a proper role for her to play," said Patchanee Arinchayawat, a junior at Chiang Mai University.
"She obviously has strong compassion for the issues. If she continues to use her prominence to promote women's rights around the world, it would be good."
In her speech at the university, Mrs Clinton called for greater efforts to improve women's rights around the world.

"At time of such momentous change on every continent, investments in people, especially women and children, are key to sustaining our progress economically and socially," she told around 4,000 people who gave her a standing ovation.
"No country can move forward into the 21st century if half its population is left on the margins," she said.
